We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

We have guidance: steps are SN2, Friedel-Crafts acylation, substitution (halogen to something). The forward reactions are enumerated in order they must be applied. So retrosynthesis: we need to break target into precursors via reverse of those steps.

Probably step 1 (last forward) is SN2: C-N formed, C-Cl broken. So in retrosynthesis we replace a C-N bond with C-Cl (or C-Br). Identify a C-N bond in target that could be formed via SN2. Likely the side chain Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to the triazine? Actually target: anilide attached to heterocycle. The side chain: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 is a benzyl attached to triazine nitrogen? The triazine (c2nnn(... )c2N) has a substituent Cc3... attached to N? The SMILES: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N. So the triazine has an N-alkyl substituent (benzyl) and an exocyclic NH (N). The benzyl group could be introduced via SN2 from benzyl chloride reacting with amine (N). So retrosynthesis: replace the N-CH2-aryl with N-CH2-Cl? Actually SN2: nucleophile attacks electrophilic carbon, leaving group halide leaves. So forward SN2: N attacks benzyl chloride to give N-CH2-aryl. So retrosynthesis: break N-CH2 bond to give amine (NH) and benzyl chloride.

Thus first disconnection: target -> amine (the triazine with NH) + benzyl chloride (or benzyl bromide). The amine is the triazine core with NH (c2nnn(c2N)??). So we need to generate that.

Second step: Friedel-Crafts acylation: maybe to install the amide linking the aniline to the heterocycle. The target has an anilide: COc1cccc(NC(=O)...)c1. So forward Friedel-Crafts acylation would attach acyl group onto aromatic ring via acyl chloride. In retrosynthesis, we break the C-C bond between aromatic ring and carbonyl, giving aniline (with OMe) and acyl chloride (or acid chloride). So we get 4-methoxy-aniline (or anisidine) and acyl chloride derived from heterocycle (c2nnn...). So second disconnection: target -> anisidine (COc1cccc(NH2?) actually the aniline after removal of acyl) and acyl chloride of heterocycle.

Third step: substitution reaction to replace a leaving group (like OH) with halogen. Possibly to convert a phenol to aryl halide for Friedel-Crafts? Or to convert a carboxylic acid to acyl chloride? The guidance says substitution to replace hydroxyl with halogen using reagents like SOCl2. So maybe we need to convert a phenol (or carboxylic acid) to aryl halide for later steps. In our route, we need the acyl chloride precursor. Starting from a carboxylic acid (or acid) we can convert to acyl chloride via substitution (Cl). So third step: from heterocycle carboxylic acid (or maybe from amide?) to acyl chloride.

Thus propose route:

Step 1 (retro SN2): target -> intermediate A (triazine core with NH) + benzyl chloride (ClCH2-Ph-...?). Actually benzyl chloride with para-substituted phenyl bearing N4CC(F)C4? The benzyl chloride is 4-(N4CC(F)C4)phenylmethyl chloride. So we need that as a precursor.

Step 2 (retro Friedel-Crafts acylation): intermediate A + anisidine (4-methoxyaniline) from target? Wait the amide bond is between anisidine nitrogen and carbonyl attached to triazine. So after SN2 step, we have intermediate A which is the amide attached to anisidine? Actually the SN2 step is on the side chain attached to triazine, not the amide. So after SN2 disconnection, we still have the amide linking anisidine to triazine. So intermediate after step1 is: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1 but with N-CH2 replaced by N-H? Wait the SN2 bond is N-CH2 (the benzyl). So after breaking, we get COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1? Actually the benzyl is attached to the triazine via N-CH2-aryl. So after cleavage, the triazine will have N-H (instead of N-CH2-aryl). So intermediate B: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1 where the N attached to benzyl is now NH (i.e., the triazine has an NH substituent). But the SMILES already shows c2nnn(... )c2N meaning there is an exocyclic N attached to triazine (maybe NH). The benzyl is attached to the N of the triazine? Actually the SMILES: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N. The N at end is exocyclic N (attached to triazine). The substituent Cc3... is attached to the N of the triazine? The pattern nnn(Cc3...) indicates the N of the triazine is attached to the benzyl. So the triazine has two substituents: one is the benzyl (via N) and the other is an exocyclic NH (c2N). So SN2 could be formation of N-CH2 bond from N (as nucleophile) and benzyl halide. So retro SN2 gives triazine with NH (exocyclic) and benzyl halide.

Thus intermediate after step1: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(c2N)?? Actually the benzyl removed, leaving just c2nnn(c2N)?? The SMILES would be COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(c2N)c2N?) Wait need to adjust. The triazine after removal of benzyl substituent will have a hydrogen on that N (so N-H). So the triazine core becomes c2nnn(NH)c2N? Actually the N that had benzyl becomes NH. So the heterocycle becomes c2nnn(NH)c2N (i.e., a diaminotriazine). So intermediate B: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(NH)c2N)c1.

Step2 retro Friedel-Crafts: break amide bond between anisidine and carbonyl, giving anisidine (4-methoxyaniline) and acyl chloride derived from diaminotriazine (i.e., ClC(=O)-c2nnn(NH)c2N). So intermediate C: 4-methoxyaniline (COc1cccc(NH2)c1) and acyl chloride.

Step3 retro substitution: convert acyl chloride from maybe carboxylic acid precursor. Starting from diaminotriazine carboxylic acid (c2nnn(NH)c2N-COOH). So substitution of OH to Cl (via SOCl2). So final precursor D: diaminotriazine carboxylic acid.

Thus we have 3 steps.

Now we need to find template IDs for each reaction. Use search to find templates matching these transformations.

First, SN2: N-CH2 bond formation from N nucleophile and benzyl halide. Search for template where functional groups formed: C-N, broken: halide. Use functional_groups_formed "secondary amines"? The N is secondary after substitution? The nucleophile is amine (primary) reacting with benzyl halide to give secondary amine. So functional group formed: secondary amine. Let's search.
